text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm trying to lock down per-GPU targets for max_batch_size and max_tokens_per_batch for continuous batching. Experiment run notes attached below. TL;DR: raising tokens cap improved throughput on A100/H100 but gave kernel-fallback and KV-frag regressions on T4/L4 for long contexts. Need a rollout plan.

devon: paste the key numbers? esp. 95p latency, and any throughput rps delta.

maria: brief paste: 
```
configs tested: baseline (tokens_cap=64k, batch_slots=64) vs higher-cap (tokens_cap=128k, batch_slots=128)
A100 (gpt-13b): throughput +27% (p50), p95 latency -12% on high-cap, memory headroom ok
H100 (gpt-70b): throughput +35%, p95 -18% but KV cache occupancy jumped ~22% -> more fragmentation
A10: throughput +9%, p95 ~same, some kernel selector falls back for long seqs
T4/L4: small throughput gains (~3-6%) but p95 regressed up to +20% for mixed short+long routes
observed kernel fallbacks when contiguous KV buffer > ~48k tokens -> choose conservative caps per device
```

ajay: re: KV fragmentation — when we let larger token bundles through, KV cache allocs become non-contiguous and trigger path that uses generic matmul kernels. That is the main cause of p95 regressions on T4/L4. Also observed higher L2 thrash on L4.

nora: suggestion: enforce "token-first" cap in queue policy. i.e. prefer forming batches up to max_tokens_per_batch, but never exceed device-specific token cap. Then enforce a stricter max_batch_size for smaller GPUs. Pseudoconfig: 
```
batching_policy:
  order: token_first
  device_profiles:
    H100: { max_batch_size: "128", max_tokens_per_batch: "131072" }
    A100: { max_batch_size: "96",  max_tokens_per_batch: "65536" }
    A10:  { max_batch_size: "48",  max_tokens_per_batch: "32768" }
    L4:   { max_batch_size: "24",  max_tokens_per_batch: "16384" }
    T4:   { max_batch_size: "16",  max_tokens_per_batch: "8192" }
```
Keep these as defaults but allow model overrides for long-context models.

samir: +1 to per-device caps but we need a safe rollout. Proposal: canary lane (5% traffic) with perf regression detector (p95 up >8% or error-rate up >0.5% -> abort). Also add kernel-selection telemetry to alert when fallback rate >3%.

perf-bot: experiment-summary: canary-run=100k requests across mixed routes: H100 high-cap success rate 99.98%, p95 -16%; T4 high-cap abort (p95 +21% -> triggered rollback). Kernel-fallback-rate: H100 1.2%, A100 2.9%, A10 4.8%, L4 6.3%, T4 12.7%.

ajay: those fallback rates explain it. For T4/L4 we should keep token caps low and favor slot-based batching. Also look into kernel selector: current threshold for switching to generic kernels is contiguous-KV > 48k tokens; we can try tunables: increase fragmentation threshold for H100/A100 only.

maria: agree. Implementation plan:
- publish device_profiles as nora suggested (defaults only)
- add model-level overrides (long-context models)
- canary rollout: H100/A100 -> 5% first wave; A10/L4/T4 -> keep baseline until kernel selector improvements or KV compaction implemented
- add perf alerts: kernel-fallback-rate and KV-frag metric -> auto-abort on canary

ops-bot: scheduling canary rollout: scheduled 2026-06-02T03:30:00Z to 03:45:00Z for H100/A100 lanes. Automated abort hooks enabled.

devon: one more ask — do we have a small microbenchmark to reproduce KV fragmentation locally? would help iterate on kernel selector thresholds.

maria: yes, I pushed a repro harness to eng-runtime/playgrounds/kv-frag-harness. Basic command: `./run_kv_frag_test --gpu A100 --tokens 70000 --seqs 8`. It spits out per-kernel runtime and malloc fragmentation stats.

nora: will try the harness and then raise PR for device_profiles config + canary job.

maria: great — thanks everyone. I'll draft the rollout runbook and add the abort criteria. :thumbsup:
